propositions: The existing checker (R1/R2) enforces no-raw-subprocess-git but misses protocol violations: mutation primitives exported from git_adapter.py are sanctioned per-call, allowing unapproved callers to compose them outside the atomic transaction seam.

Rule R3 (seam composition) must fire when a git-adapter mutation primitive (add, commit, commit_tree, read_tree, rm_cached, update_ref, write_tree) is called from outside the sanctioned seam files (git_adapter.py, _ref_lock.py, _ref_lock_push.py), with binding resolution via import statements and dynamic loaders.

Two out-of-transaction sites must receive durable reasoned inline markers: reconcile_helpers.py:226/246 (selective staging boundary preventing routing through seam) and __main__.py:338-351 (detached-index CAS migration, concurrency-safe by construction).
R3 must not fire on non-git-adapter .add/.commit calls (set, session) or read-only exports (commit_email), and must not produce false positives across src/ and scripts/ in a dry-run enumeration.
A reasoned # raw-git-ok: marker (line-level or function-level) sanctions an R3 violation; a bare marker without reason must still fail as marker-without-reason.

The gate must land after parallel remediations (blockers gnatty-comparable-ynambu and cubiform-wooden-fruitbat) close to avoid merge-conflict churn and ensure zero enumerated out-of-transaction sites at first run, plus the __main__.py module-size split preserves all patch targets and seam-clean proofs.
